safety.en: Paths and quieter countryside offer breathing room, with road sections, crossings and uneven ground still needing attention.

scenery.en: Lakes, woodland and rolling hills make this a lovely setting for a varied outing.

surface.en: The mix of forest paths, gravel and asphalt suits varied training better than a consistent road pace.

experience.en: The enjoyable lake run and varied Vidrike hike made a strong combination for exploring the area on foot.

en.title: Otepää: trails and rolling hills
en.excerpt: A Pühajärv lake run, a longer hike around Vidrike and plenty of hills: two routes for exploring Estonia’s winter capital without the snow.

practicalSummary.goodFor: Rolling hill training, a lake loop and longer outings over mixed terrain.
practicalSummary.terrain: Forest paths, gravel and asphalt, with frequent short climbs and descents.
practicalSummary.keepInMind: Long flat stretches take some finding; I completed the longer Vidrike route as a hike, not a run.

en.body:
If you grow up around Otepää and enjoy sport, there is a fair chance that skiing or another winter sport will become part of your life. It is [Estonia’s winter capital](https://visitestonia.com/en/where-to-go/otepaa-a-winter-capital-for-all-seasons), but the same rolling hills make it a very good place to train when the snow is gone.

For running, that means plenty of climbs and descents, lakes, forest and quieter countryside. Finding a long flat stretch takes a little more effort. There are gentler sections, but I would come here expecting the terrain to keep changing.

![A rolling asphalt road curving between green hills and trees at Mäha near Otepää](/assets/uploads/otepaa-puhajarv-vidrike/maha-asphalt-road.jpg "An asphalt road at Mäha, near Otepää, illustrating the local countryside rather than a specific section of my GPX. Photo: [Toomas Tsamoot](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:M%C3%A4ha_-_panoramio.jpg) · [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0).")

## Pühajärv: a lap of the lake

One of the routes I am sharing is from the Pühajärve lake race, starting beside Pühajärve Spa hotel. It is a very enjoyable loop with enough hills and descents to keep it interesting, rather than ten kilometres of holding exactly the same rhythm.

The [organiser lists the race as 10.7 km](https://stamina.ee/et/tondiraba/info-ja-juhend?action=guide_by_id&competition_id=298&guide_id=172), with approximately 110 m of climbing (my GPX data). The opening part is more undulating and much of the later part sits lower and is gentler, although the profile still has smaller rises.

This is the lake-race route, rather than a promise that every path around Pühajärv follows the same line. There are other walking options nearby too, including the Murrumets forest paths.

![Elevation profile of the 10.6 km Pühajärve lake loop](/assets/uploads/otepaa-puhajarv-vidrike/puhajarve-lake-run-profile.svg "10.6 km for the full loop, with about 110 m of climbing; small elevation fluctuations are smoothed.")

## Rännak ja Rüübe: a hike I would run

The second route comes from a hike I did during [Rännak ja Rüübe (literally means ''Hike and Drink'' and yes, you can have wine at every stop during the hike)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DXW5dvQl_C6/), an event organised by the family behind Vidrike Külamaja. I am including it because it struck me as a really good running option too: a mixture of paths, gravel roads and asphalt, with hills, descents and some lovely views.

I walked this one, so I am not presenting it as a completed training run. My track adds up to 18.8 km, with approximately 200 m of climbing, with stops including Sokka, Toidupada, Vidrike Külamaja, Klaasivabrik Vidrike and [Murimäe winery](https://murimaevein.ee/).

The terrain rolls almost throughout. Two more noticeable uphill sections follow the lower points around 10 km and 15 km, with the later rise continuing towards roughly 17 km. There are easier sections between them, but this is more of a varied countryside loop than a place for uninterrupted flat intervals.

![Elevation profile of the 18.8 km Rännak ja Rüübe hiking loop](/assets/uploads/otepaa-puhajarv-vidrike/vidrike-rannak-ja-ruube-profile.svg "18.8 km for the full hiking loop, with about 200 m of climbing from smoothed GPX elevations.")

For anyone who likes trail running, this is the option I would look at first out of these two. I would use the line below to plan an independent outing, while remembering that the event’s food stops and arrangements do not automatically exist on another day.

## Vidrike: Italian food and lake views

[Vidrike Külamaja](https://www.kylamaja.ee/) deserves a mention beyond the hike. The restaurant has built a reputation for Italian food, and the setting beside the lake is a very good reason to spend some time here after exploring the surrounding countryside.

![Pancakes cooking beside the lake, alongside the Rännak ja Rüübe event map](/assets/uploads/otepaa-puhajarv-vidrike/vidrike-pancakes-and-event-map.webp "The Vidrike family also made delicious pancakes that morning, with a lovely view over the lake.")

## Tehvandi: winter hills without the snow

Another option to look at in Otepää is [Tehvandi’s 5 km running and Nordic walking trail](https://visitestonia.com/en/tehvandi-running-and-nordic-walking-trail). The marked route has demanding climbs and descents, with sawdust on part of the surface; take care where it crosses roller-ski tracks. It is separate from my two GPX routes below.

![Tehvandi stadium with a blue running track and wooded hills in the background](/assets/uploads/otepaa-puhajarv-vidrike/tehvandi-stadium.jpg "Tehvandi stadium in May 2013, with the hills behind it. Photo: [Santeri Viinamäki](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tehvandi_suusastaadion_May_2013.jpg) · [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0).")

Tehvandi is also Otepää’s biathlon venue: it hosted a World Cup round in 2026 and is preparing for the [2027 Biathlon World Championships](https://www.biathlonotepaa.com/en). The hills that work the skiers hard are very much part of the appeal here outside winter too.

For me, the attraction around Otepää is the variety. A lake loop, a longer mixed-surface outing and plenty of hills to train on: there is a lot here for runners who enjoy changing terrain. I would simply choose a shorter option first if hills are still new to me.
